questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Mexico?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mexico article.

questions.proof: Mexico City is the capital and largest city, which ranks among the most populous metropolitan areas in the world.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Mexico?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People” part of the Mexico article.

questions.proof: Mexico is the most populous Spanish-speaking country in the world.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Juarez stayed president until _____ invaded Mexico and made Maximilian of Habsburg emperor of the Second Mexican Empire.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “until”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Mexico article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Juarez stayed president until France invaded Mexico and made Maximilian of Habsburg emperor of the Second Mexican Empire.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is also the second most populous country in Latin America (after _____).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “America”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Mexico article, under the heading “People”.

questions.proof: It is also the second most populous country in Latin America (after Brazil).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “But the Mexicans were not happy with him, and in _____ the country became a republic.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Mexico article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: But the Mexicans were not happy with him, and in 1823 the country became a republic.
